newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SIA equipped to face competition - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: SIA equipped to face competition - Salomon.

text.p: Singapore Airlines Ltd's strong balance sheet and management should allow it to cope with rising competition and a strong Singapore dollar, although 1997 and 1998 earnings are set to lag the market, Salomon Brothers said.

In a statement issued in Hong Kong following the release of a recent report, Salomon said Singapore Airlines' (SIA) yields have dropped by an average 5.2 percent annually since 1989 due to competitive pressures and a strong Singapore dollar. At the same time, costs have fallen at a rate of 4.2 percent.
"A similar trend is likely to continue over the coming years," Salomon said in the report.

"In consideration of these factors, we forecast a 1.1 percent and 9.6 percent earnings growth in fiscal 1997 and 1998, respectively, which is below Salomon Brothers' forecast for the Singapore market," it added.
But the investment bank maintained a hold rating on foreign shares due to the company's strong financial condition and market position.

"SIA's financial position is beyond comparison among other major listed global airline stocks. It has had zero net debt position since 1988, which means through the economic cycle its earnings should show less volatility as it does not incur a net interest charge," Salomon said.
It said a heavy aircraft delivery schedule during the current year may require SIA to raise some short-term funds.
"However, we estimate there will be surplus cash flow in fiscal 1998, bringing the company back to a net cash position," Salomon said.
Gains from aircraft sales and capital gains on investment are expected to account for about 14 percent of pretax earnings in fiscal 1997 and 1998, it added.
